assessments.reasoning: I checked the publisher's verified v3.13.0 tag against its exact commit, independently fetched the exact official file over HTTPS, and verified its byte digest. I read the frozen cited passage (The nonlocal statement, lines 1001–1023). The nonlocal statement section at 1001–1023 gives the function-scope rule in general terms. The two cited chapters describe the enclosing-function rule and its lexical and annotation-scope conditions. The stated scope fails to account for the implicit class cell documented in the same edition's data model, lines 2609–2622. The pinned compiler at symtable.c lines 1127–1132 inserts __class__ for children of a class, and lines 644–673 accept a visible name as free even if no function bound it. CPython 3.13.5 accepted the syntax nonlocal __class__ in a method of a module-level class and returned Holder even with no enclosing function local. A method of a class nested in a function that binds __class__ still returned Holder. The exact 3.13.0 compiler source explains the inserted class cell. Function shadowing, global masking, annotation exclusion and late binding otherwise behaved as expected.
